\[
\rho = x \cos\theta + y \sin\theta,
\qquad
H(\theta, \rho) = \#\{\text{edge pixels on the line } (\theta, \rho)\}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\theta\): The angle of the normal of a line
- \(\rho\): The distance of a line from the origin
- \(H\): The accumulator of votes

A line is described by the angle theta of its normal and its distance rho from the origin, as Duda and Hart proposed. An edge pixel at (x, y) lies on all lines with x cos theta + y sin theta = rho, which is a sine curve in the plane of theta and rho. Every edge pixel adds one vote along its curve in the accumulator H. Where many curves cross, many edge pixels lie on one line, so peaks of H are lines. Here scikit-image measures theta with y pointing down and the origin at the center of the top-left pixel. The peaks must reach the vote threshold times the largest vote and lie apart by the distance and angle limits.
